prompt: The shop wants its web machines spread over the three zones of `brazilsouth`. How many subnets does that take in `vnet-shop-prod`?
hint: Where does an Azure subnet live?

choices.text: Three, one per zone, since a subnet sits in a single zone
choices.why: That is the picture other clouds draw. An Azure subnet spans every zone of its region.

choices.text: None until a second region is added
choices.why: A VNet lives in one region and its subnets in all of that region's zones.

choices.text: Six, a public and a private one in each zone
choices.why: Neither zones nor public and private multiply subnets here.

choices.text: One: a subnet spans every zone
choices.why: Right. The machines choose their zones; the subnet is in all of them.

prompt: The office says it uses `10.0.0.0/8` and wants a VPN to Azure. Why does the lesson call that a trap?
hint: Look at the last line of the overlap check.

choices.text: Because `10.0.0.0/8` is not a private range
choices.why: It is the largest of the three private ranges of RFC 1918.

choices.text: Because Azure accepts only `/16` networks from an office
choices.why: No such limit exists. The size is not the problem; what it covers is.

choices.text: It overlaps every `10.` network the shop has in Azure
choices.why: Right. A `/8` contains every `/16` that starts with `10.`, so no address can be told apart.

choices.text: Because a VPN carries only one `/24` at a time
choices.why: A VPN carries whatever ranges both sides route.

prompt: Which address can never be part of a VNet's range?
hint: Azure itself answers on it inside every network.

choices.why: Right. Azure's DNS and health checks answer there, so it is refused.
The shared space of RFC 6598 is accepted and treated as private.
A private address; only the office's use of the range keeps the shop out of it.
It is a network address inside a private range, and `vnet-shop-prod` starts with it.

prompt: What does a VNet with four subnets and nothing in it cost per month?
hint: What is billed in a network?

choices.text: A fixed fee per subnet
choices.why: Subnets are free. The bill comes from what is placed in them.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right. What costs is what you put in it and connect it to.

choices.text: A fee per address in the range, used or not
choices.why: Private addresses are not billed.

choices.text: The same as a small virtual machine, as a network runs on one
choices.why: A VNet is not a machine; it is rules about addresses.

prompt: How many usable addresses does Azure leave in a `/27` subnet?
hint: A `/27` holds 32.

prompt: Match each address of `snet-app`, `10.20.2.0/24`, to what Azure uses it for.

pairs.right: the first address a machine can get

prompt: `plan.py` refused `snet-jobs=10.20.7.0/23` with *has host bits set*. What is wrong with the range?
hint: Where can a `/23` start?

choices.text: It overlaps `snet-web`
choices.why: `snet-web` is `10.20.1.0/24`, far below it.

choices.text: It starts on an odd third number
It is smaller than Azure's minimum
choices.why: A `/23` holds 512 addresses; the minimum is a `/29`.

choices.text: It falls outside `10.20.0.0/16`
choices.why: Every `10.20.` address is inside the network.

prompt: Why does the shop leave over 98% of `10.20.0.0/16` in no subnet at all?
hint: When can a subnet be resized?

choices.text: A subnet resizes only while empty, so room is left now
choices.why: Right. New tiers and services get fresh ranges instead of a rebuild.

choices.text: Because a VNet may hold at most four subnets
choices.why: A VNet holds many more; four is the shop's plan, not a limit.

choices.text: Because the rest is kept for the paired region
choices.why: A VNet's range is not shared with any region.

choices.text: Because Azure bills each address placed in a subnet
choices.why: Subnets and their addresses are free.

prompt: A team deploys Azure Firewall into a `/24` it named `snet-firewall`. What happens?
hint: What is the contract between the service and the subnet?

choices.text: Azure renames the subnet on deployment
choices.why: Nothing renames a subnet for you.

choices.text: It works, since a `/24` is larger than the `/26` asked for
choices.why: Size is necessary and not enough; the name is checked too.

choices.text: Azure refuses it: the subnet must be called `AzureFirewallSubnet`
choices.why: Right. The name is the contract, whatever the size.

choices.text: The firewall is placed in a hidden subnet of its own
choices.why: Azure Firewall goes in the VNet's own `AzureFirewallSubnet`, which you create.

prompt: The smallest IPv4 subnet Azure allows is a `/___`, with three usable addresses.
hint: Eight addresses, five of them taken.

prompt: What does delegating `snet-data` to `Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers` allow?
hint: Who gets to place things in the subnet?

choices.text: Any PostgreSQL client to connect from the internet
choices.why: Delegation is about who may build in the subnet, not who may connect to it.

choices.text: The subnet to be shared with another subscription
choices.why: Delegation is to a service, not to a subscription.

choices.text: The database to take addresses from every subnet of the VNet
choices.why: Only the delegated subnet is the service's.

choices.text: The service to create and manage what it needs in that subnet
choices.why: Right. It may also set network rules there that you cannot remove while it is there.

prompt: Why does `vnet.bicep` write the subnets inside the network instead of as separate resources?
hint: What happens when the network alone is deployed again?

choices.text: Bicep refuses subnets declared as separate resources
choices.why: Bicep allows both forms.

choices.text: Separate subnets would cost extra
choices.why: Subnets cost nothing in either form.

choices.text: Delegation works only on subnets written inside
choices.why: A delegation is a property of the subnet in either form.

choices.text: Redeploying the network alone keeps them
choices.why: Right. A network file that leaves them out can describe a network with no subnets.

prompt: `outside.bicep` put `snet-pe` at `10.99.4.0/24`, outside the network, and compiled. What does that show?
hint: What does the compiler check about a string?

choices.text: That Azure accepts subnets outside their network
choices.why: Azure would refuse the deployment; it was the compiler that said nothing.

choices.text: That `addressPrefix` is ignored when `addressSpace` is set
choices.why: Both are kept in the template, as the output showed.

choices.text: The compiler checks types, not the arithmetic of addresses
choices.why: Right. That is the job `plan.py` does before anybody deploys.

choices.text: That the range is moved inside the network on deployment
choices.why: Nothing moves a range for you.

prompt: A pipeline compiles `typo.bicep`, sees a zero exit code and deploys. The file says `defaultOutbondAccess: false`. What does the subnet get?
hint: What became of the misspelt property?

choices.text: Its API version's default, not what the file meant
choices.why: Right. Read the warnings, or make them errors in `bicepconfig.json`.

choices.text: Nothing: the build failed and nothing was deployed
choices.why: BCP089 is a warning; the build succeeded.

choices.text: A subnet with no address range at all
choices.why: The range was spelt correctly and survives.

choices.text: A private subnet, since Bicep corrected the name
choices.why: Bicep suggested the right name and wrote the wrong one into the template.

hint: The function that returns the n-th slice of a range.

prompt: What does `defaultOutboundAccess: false` change for a machine in `snet-app`?
hint: Which way out is left?

choices.text: It cannot be reached from the rest of the VNet
choices.why: Traffic inside the network is unaffected.

choices.text: Only a route built on purpose takes it out
choices.why: Right. The firewall of lesson 18 is that route for the shop.

choices.text: It loses its private address
choices.why: Private addresses are untouched.

choices.text: It may receive traffic from the internet on any port
choices.why: It is about leaving, and it closes a door rather than opening one.

prompt: Put the steps of building `vnet-shop-prod` in the order the lesson takes them.
hint: The range comes before anything is cut from it.
items: choose a range that overlaps no network the shop will connect
write the network and its subnets in `vnet.bicep`
compile it and read the subnets back
trap: Compiling comes last, and still does not check the arithmetic: `plan.py` did that.

prompt: Staging is `10.30.0.0/16`. A developer creates a test network at `10.30.128.0/17` in another subscription, to be peered with production next month. What goes wrong?

choices.text: It overlaps staging, so those two will never be joined
choices.why: Right. Production peers with it, and the day staging needs it too, the two collide.

choices.text: The peering with production fails, since a `/17` cannot peer
choices.why: Any size can peer; the size is not the issue.

choices.text: Nothing, as long as it is in another subscription
choices.why: Overlap is about addresses, not about who owns them.

choices.text: Azure refuses to create it, since `10.30.` belongs to staging
choices.why: Azure checks overlap only when two networks are connected.
